# Baruch Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Take off, O Jerusalem, the garment of your mourning and affliction, and put on the beauty of the glory from God forever.

**2** Clothe yourself with the double garment of the righteousness from God; put on your head the diadem of the glory of the Eternal.

**3** For God will show your splendor to every nation under heaven.

**4** For your name will forever be called by God: Peace of righteousness and glory of godliness.

**5** Arise, O Jerusalem, and stand upon the height, and look toward the east, and see your children gathered from the rising of the sun to its setting, at the word of the Holy One, rejoicing that God has remembered them.

**6** For they went out from you on foot, led away by enemies; but God is bringing them back to you, carried in glory, as on a royal throne.

**7** For God has ordered that every high mountain and the everlasting hills be made low, and that the valleys be filled up, to level the ground, so that Israel may walk safely in the glory of God.

**8** The woods and every fragrant tree have overshadowed Israel at God's command.

**9** For God will lead Israel with joy, in the light of his glory, with the mercy and the righteousness that come from him.

---
*EMET notes: v.1 "the garment of your mourning" reverses v.4:20 "robe of peace" — the bookending is deliberate. v.2 "double garment" — Greek diploidia = double cloak. The compound phrase "righteousness and glory" as divine clothing echoes Isa 61:10. v.4 the new name — "Peace of righteousness and glory of godliness" — is a formal divine renaming echoing Isa 62:2-4. v.7 "high mountain... hills made low... valleys filled" is a close echo of Isa 40:4 and Luke 3:5. This is one of the clearest intertextual links in the entire Deuterocanon. v.9 "light of his glory" — a pillar of glory replaces the pillar of cloud/fire from the Exodus.*
